notes: Deliberately excludes require-lock-timeout/require-statement-timeout equivalents (squawk's rules): those describe how the runner opens its session, not what the SQL says. RUN-02 makes the Phase 4 runner responsible for setting them on every migration; a rule flagging every migration for a property the runner already guarantees would be a false positive by construction (03-CONTEXT.md D-04).

rules.rationale: DROP TABLE permanently destroys the table and every row it holds; there is no automated way to recover the data afterward.
DROP SCHEMA permanently destroys every object inside the schema, including all of its tables and their data.
DROP DATABASE permanently destroys the entire database, every schema and table in it.
TRUNCATE removes every row from a table in a single unrecoverable operation, bypassing per-row triggers and any WHERE-based scoping.
DROP COLUMN permanently destroys every value stored in that column across every row.
A DELETE with no WHERE clause removes every row in the table, which is almost never the intended scope of a migration.
An UPDATE with no WHERE clause overwrites every row in the table, which is almost never the intended scope of a migration.

Dropping an enum value permanently removes it from the type and destroys any row still carrying it, with no automated way to recover the value afterward. PostgreSQL's own grammar rejects this statement outright today (confirmed live against libpg-query@17.7.4: it always raises 'dropping an enum value is not implemented' at parse time), so this rule can never currently fire -- it is kept as documentation of FEATURES.md section 1's BLOCKED entry and as a floor should a future PostgreSQL version ever implement the operation.
A volatile default (e.g. clock_timestamp(), gen_random_uuid()) cannot be stored as a single metadata value, so PostgreSQL rewrites the entire table and its indexes under ACCESS EXCLUSIVE.
SET NOT NULL on an existing column forces a full table scan under ACCESS EXCLUSIVE to verify no NULLs exist, blocking reads and writes for the scan's duration.

ALTER COLUMN TYPE always takes ACCESS EXCLUSIVE, and this analyzer has no database connection to know whether the change is a safe widening or a lossy narrowing, so the lossiness question goes to a human.
Adding a UNIQUE constraint without USING INDEX builds its backing index while holding ACCESS EXCLUSIVE for the entire build, blocking reads and writes on the table.
Building an index without CONCURRENTLY takes a SHARE lock on the table for the whole build, blocking every INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE until it finishes.
Dropping an index without CONCURRENTLY takes ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on the table for the drop, which can queue behind and then block every other lock request on it.
A plainly added foreign key scans and locks both the altering table and the referenced table while validating every existing row, unlike the NOT VALID plus VALIDATE CONSTRAINT two-step form.
Renaming a column is an instant metadata change with no lock hazard, but any application code still referencing the old name breaks immediately during a rolling deploy's compatibility window.
Renaming a table is an instant metadata change with no lock hazard, but any application code still referencing the old name breaks immediately during a rolling deploy's compatibility window.
Dropping a NOT NULL constraint is metadata-only with no lock hazard, but it silently changes what application code can rely on being present, breaking any code that assumed the column was never null.

Dropping a constraint is metadata-only with no lock hazard, but whether any application code depends on the guarantee it enforced is an application-level fact this analyzer cannot verify from the database alone.
Creating a brand new table has no existing rows to lock, scan or rewrite, and no application code can yet depend on it.
Adding a nullable column with no default is a metadata-only change that requires no table rewrite and no scan of existing rows.

A non-volatile default (a literal, or an IMMUTABLE or STABLE function such as now()) is evaluated once and stored in the table's own metadata, so PostgreSQL's fast add-column path applies and no rewrite is required.
CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY takes only SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE, letting concurrent reads and writes continue for almost the entire build.
DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY takes only SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE, letting concurrent reads and writes continue for almost the entire drop.
COMMENT ON only updates catalog metadata text, taking no meaningful lock and touching no row in the table it describes.
A check constraint added NOT VALID is instant and enforces only on new or changed rows, deferring the table scan to a separate, weaker-locked VALIDATE CONSTRAINT step.
A foreign key added NOT VALID is instant and enforces only on new or changed rows, deferring the scan of both tables to a separate, weaker-locked VALIDATE CONSTRAINT step.
VALIDATE CONSTRAINT takes only SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE on the altered table, letting concurrent reads and writes continue while it scans for constraint violations.

The analyzer found no executable statement in this migration file (empty, whitespace-only, or comment-only input). SAFE must be earned by a matching rule (D-06), and a migration file with nothing executable in it is anomalous enough to be worth a human glance.

The constraint was added NOT VALID (instant, no scan) and later validated by its own VALIDATE CONSTRAINT statement (SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE only) naming the exact same constraint in this same file -- the complete two-step safe form for adding a validated constraint without ever taking a table-scanning lock. This rule id is applied only by the applySafeFormPairing pass (classify.ts), never by ordinary per-statement matching: its match object (ValidateConstraint with notValid true) can never be satisfied by a real finding, because PostgreSQL's grammar has no NOT VALID form of VALIDATE CONSTRAINT -- this entry exists purely so the pairing pass can look up a stable id and this rationale, the same way D-03 requires of every other rule.

The unique index backing this constraint was already built CONCURRENTLY (SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE only) in this same file, so attaching it via ADD CONSTRAINT ... UNIQUE USING INDEX is a metadata-only operation -- the complete two-step safe form for adding a unique constraint without blocking writes during the index build. This rule id is applied only by the applySafeFormPairing pass: its match object (AddUniqueConstraint with concurrently true) can never be satisfied by a real finding, because the inspector never sets `concurrently` for an AddUniqueConstraint fact (only CreateIndex/DropIndex carry that flag) -- this entry exists purely for pairing's id/rationale lookup, per D-03.

A CHECK (col IS NOT NULL) constraint proving this exact column non-nullable was already added and validated in this same file, so PostgreSQL 12+ detects the validated check constraint and skips SET NOT NULL's own table scan -- the complete safe form for enforcing NOT NULL without an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE scan. This rule id is applied only by the applySafeFormPairing pass: its match object (SetNotNull with checkProvesNotNull true) can never be satisfied by a real finding, because the inspector never sets `checkProvesNotNull` for a SetNotNull fact (only AddCheckConstraint's branch touches that field) -- this entry exists purely for pairing's id/rationale lookup, per D-03.
